obligations.statement: Amounts and limits use exact specified integer units with checked decimal conversion, precision, overflow and target-asset representability. Signed-to-unsigned chain-clock conversion is checked; negative timestamps cannot wrap.

Approval, executor, revision, parameters, spending/day and time come from authenticated current state; stale, revoked, foreign or caller-forged authority cannot execute. Separate editor/server revision, on-chain state/parameter revision and standing module approval; none substitutes for another.
A successful operation transfers exactly the bound asset, amount and recipient from the intended vault and commits spending/replay atomically; rejection leaves protected state unchanged.

Each accepted transfer records the authenticated execution day and exact effective spending within that execution's limit; only legitimate day advancement supplies a fresh allowance, with no skipped-day accumulation. Adapter day/reset arithmetic must agree with kernel DAY_SECONDS and returned next spending; persist that day and result without a divergent second definition.
Deposit/top-up changes only declared custody effects and never approval, code/parameter revision, limit, spending/day or replay identity.

Authorized tuning changes only the declared daily-limit parameter within compiled bounds; it preserves accounting/replay and handles a limit below already-spent without reset. Source authoring does not introduce extra mutable native parameters. Under the announced native handoff, owner-authorized bounded tuning preserves standing module approval and counters, advances state/parameter revision and invalidates old unsigned request revisions; the ceiling is independently anchored in custody state or the verified artifact, not merely reported by a candidate module.

Approved code/revision transitions preserve custody/accounting identity, balances, spending/day and replay under an explicit migration relation; old requests cannot silently gain new authority. In-place module switching withdraws standing approval and preserves counters. MVP enforcement-code replacement is a new reviewed activation: retire old standing execution authority before authorizing the replacement, retain old funds/counters/recovery identities, and disclose the replacement vault's separate daily allowance.
Concurrent operations serialize against authoritative state; duplicate/retried identities cannot transfer twice, including across day/configuration changes and restart.
Unsupported valid methods return an explicit unsupported-method error; malformed ABI input has a specified decode error; neither path mutates protected state or falls back to transfer.
Preview/eval/read/status do not transfer, reserve funds, consume replay identity, change daily accounting or approve authority; projections accurately identify their observed state.

Stable operation identity and signed proof persist before broadcast; uncertain outcomes remain unresolved; reconciliation discovers the first outcome without automatically initiating another payment. Tuning does not establish failure of an already signed request; retain its identity and uncertainty until reliable finalized or expiry/absence evidence resolves it.
Every client encodes the same supported ABI/units/bindings and maps preview, refusal, required input/signature, submission, uncertainty and finalized execution without conflating them.

obligations.statement: Every visible policy field maps to its exact enforced meaning or an explicit unsupported/separate profile; total budget, monetary review, reserve and source edits are not silently mapped to daily tuning.

Requirement extraction and descriptor/fragment closure cover supported operations/providers; unknown dependencies refuse issuance; context provenance and caller capabilities are explicit and permission is not inferred from metadata.
Selected score/toggle AST edits preserve unrelated source/normalized structure, validate ranges, reject stale/unsupported selections and refresh bindings without model regeneration.

Every semantic restriction uses the customer's Jev predicate and bound authentic evidence; missing/stale/malformed/wrong-request evidence cannot permit; inclusive configured thresholds preserve hard rules and unresolved outcomes.
Any statistical interval/calibration claim identifies labeled domain, method, risk and assumptions; otherwise explicitly report a point score and decision thresholds without a statistical guarantee.
Payment settlement and request-bound service delivery are separate outcomes; failed/retried delivery cannot authorize a second charge and provider compatibility is evidenced independently.

Proof/test receipts identify their exact statement, supported domain, assumptions, implementation connection and artifacts; affected evidence becomes stale on changes and unsupported/timeouts remain unknown. Keep host, compiled-VM, local-RPC integration and public Devnet acceptance as separate evidence domains; one cannot stand in for another.
